races.name: A McKie Builders EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Beechwood Glory
runners_data.note: Unknown style with just two starts, both over 6f on good ground — the experience in similar conditions is an asset, and finishing third last time out suggests forward progress; sits at a mark of 120 with a light campaign that leaves ability assessable only to trainer John Butler.

runners_data.name: Coul Blue
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type whose sole run came over 7f on good ground, a longer trip than today's 6f, so trip shortening is a mild query; Michael Dods sends runners in good form (3/27 in 14 days) and Lewis Edmunds takes the ride having raced just 8 days ago.

runners_data.name: Flashing Star
runners_data.note: Both starts came on soft or standard going over 5f and the horse has never encountered good ground, making the going today a genuine unknown; the step up to 6f is new too, and Mark Walford's 42-day freshener adds to the uncertainty around this hold-up type.

runners_data.name: Lone Striker
runners_data.note: Unraced debutant with no public form to assess and listed as an unknown style — trainer Phillip Makin's string has been in modest form (1/6 over 14 days) and everything about this runner is speculative until the stalls open.

runners_data.name: Mick's The Boy
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner and therefore the primary pace-setter by default; three prior runs on good ground have established his style clearly, and from his position he need not do anything extravagant — the question is whether a mark of 66 reflects his ceiling or leaves room to improve.

runners_data.name: Ponte Carlo
runners_data.note: Has raced five times showing a hold-up profile, but the surplus of rear-runners in this field means he is unlikely to find genuine space at the back and will effectively race in midfield; his STYLE_FIT of 0.92 reflects that he races out of role here, and two runs on similar going from five offer limited encouragement.

runners_data.name: Redrosecastana
runners_data.note: Another unraced debutant, unknown in style and going preference, trained by Christopher Kellett whose yard has been quiet (0/4 in 14 days); impossible to factor meaningfully into any shape analysis without a run on the board.

runners_data.name: Unbeatable Fame
runners_data.note: Two runs both on good ground over 5f, both resulting in placed-outside finishes (6th, 7th) — today's 6f is a trip extension for a hold-up type who has not yet shown the ability to close, and the Richard & Peter Fahey yard is in steady rather than sharp form.

runners_data.name: Black Cuillin
runners_data.note: Three consecutive fourth-place finishes on good ground over 5f and 6f paint a picture of a consistent but limited hold-up horse; with a STYLE_FIT of 0.90 flagging that he races out of natural role today, and Craig Lidster's yard without a win in 14 days, expectations should be measured.

runners_data.name: Roman Crystal
runners_data.note: Has run four times on good ground over 6f — always at Ayr — and has placed once, giving him clear course-and-distance credentials that no rival can match; a prominent style suits this race shape well, and the Michael & David Easterby yard is active (2/27 in 14 days) with a Billy Garritty booking.

races.paceDynamic: Mick's The Boy is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner maiden and, crucially, faces no genuine pressure from another lead-seeking type, meaning he can dictate a controlled, honest gallop from the front without being hustled into burning excess energy. Roman Crystal will track prominently just behind, providing a natural second line of cover, while the bulk of the field — Coul Blue, Flashing Star, Unbeatable Fame, Ponte Carlo, and Black Cuillin — are hold-up or midfield types who will be playing catch-up from halfway. Note that this field contains more genuine hold-up horses than can all settle comfortably at the rear; Ponte Carlo and Black Cuillin are true hold-up types redistributed into midfield on the map because they are unlikely to get their natural deep position in this shape, and their effective impact late is accordingly tempered. On good ground over six furlongs at Ayr — a flat, fair track that does not particularly flatter pure hold-up horses — this race shape strongly favours horses able to race prominently or just off the controlled pace, where they can stalk the leader and pounce without having to produce an extravagant late burst.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mick's Boy Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Mick's The Boy dictates an uncontested, measured pace and the field cannot land a decisive late blow.
scenarios.body: Mick's The Boy sets a sustainable tempo with no rival prepared to challenge him for the lead, allowing him to conserve energy through the first half before being ridden out; Roman Crystal, tracking just off the shoulder, is perfectly placed to inherit or challenge at the two-furlong pole if the leader weakens.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the lead is set up honestly and a horse just off the pace produces the decisive move entering the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Roman Crystal or Beechwood Glory, both able to race prominently, get a dream tow into contention and finish strongest of all as the front-runner starts to tie up late; the even surface at Ayr rewards those who can travel smoothly in the first three and quicken off a genuine pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a significant late run from deep.
scenarios.body: Coul Blue or Unbeatable Fame, both genuine hold-up types with clean good-ground form, would need a faster-than-expected opening half to carve through beaten rivals; given only one front-runner and a likely controlled gallop, this scenario requires pace that this race shape is unlikely to generate organically.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debut/Lightly Raced Improver
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unexposed debutants — Lone Striker or Redrosecastana — shows natural ability and takes advantage of an open maiden.
scenarios.body: A first-time starter with concealed ability could exploit an unsophisticated field if it is forward-going and benefits from the honest pace; the unknown quantities make this a fringe possibility rather than a live shape.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether any rival challenges Mick's The Boy for the lead in the early strides — if Roman Crystal or another horse disputes the front, the pace dynamic changes entirely and the controlled-pace scenario collapses.

Ponte Carlo and Black Cuillin are both genuine hold-up types likely to find themselves in midfield rather than their natural deep position; if the pace is modest, they will have too much ground to make up on the flat Ayr straight.

The two debutants — Lone Striker and Redrosecastana — are complete unknowns in terms of style and ability; a forward-breaking debutant with natural speed could disrupt the expected race shape without warning.

Roman Crystal's four runs all at Ayr over 6f on good ground represent unique course familiarity in this field — watch how his jockey Billy Garritty positions him in the opening furlong, as a prominent pitch would suit the expected shape perfectly.

Flashing Star's form came entirely on softer ground over shorter; monitor how she handles today's quicker surface — if she struggles to travel on good going, she is likely to drop away from the midfield position expected of a hold-up type.

races.name: Sunday Roast At Western House Hotel Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Hi Lord
runners_data.note: Progressive 4yo hold-up type who won over this exact 5f good-ground combination 26 days ago; sits comfortably just off the pace when the fractions are steady and has strong similar-going form (1W3P in 6 runs), making him well-suited to tracking King Of The Jungle before producing a telling late move.
runners_data.comment: Hi Lord has placed third twice in his last four starts and was a winner four starts back, showing consistent involvement at the business end; carrying 140 lb from stall one, the key question is whether he can reproduce that level on the pick of his recent form.

runners_data.name: King Of The Jungle
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner here and only confirmed pace-setter; recent dual 5f winner (good and soft) gives confidence in his effectiveness at the trip, though a 49-day absence is a mild flag and the T14 rate of 2/27 suggests the Easterby yard is not in peak form — he controls tempo but may be vulnerable in the final 100 yards.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins give King Of The Jungle solid recent momentum, though 49 days off the track introduces a fitness query, and his rating of 62 ranks him seventh of thirteen; he has run over today's trip and going, and 139 lb from stall six is the weight to assess.

runners_data.name: Harb
runners_data.note: Veteran 7yo hold-up operator for Tristan Davidson, back just seven days after his last run which is a minor concern for recovery; placed three times over this course and trip on good ground, though he is yet to win over it and the 7lb claim from Lexie Clarkson may offset some of the weight disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Harb is the top-rated runner here and brings experience over today's trip and going, with a third three starts back auguring well for this grade. Fourth last time out on a quick seven-day turnaround, he carries 136 lb from stall seven but rates the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Water Of Leith
runners_data.note: Consistent veteran hold-up horse for Jim Goldie who has been placed on good ground over 5f but without a win from 15 similar-going runs in the sample; Paul Mulrennan takes over in the saddle and the horse carries respectable 5f course credentials, though lack of a recent win is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Third three starts back shows he retains ability, and having run over today's trip and going, Water Of Leith arrives fit on 12 days' rest carrying 135 lb from stall 4 — yet to win in recent starts and a trainer firing at just 5% is the concern.

runners_data.name: Startling
runners_data.note: Remarkably consistent 4yo hold-up type wearing a hood (hg:b); three seconds and a third from last five runs, all over 5f on good-to-soft ground, and Jason Hart is a strong northern sprints jockey — the horse appears to be knocking on the door but may need the race to run to suit to finally convert.
runners_data.comment: Startling has been a model of consistency, finishing second three times and third once in her last six starts, and has run over today's trip and going — the main concern is that she remains yet to score despite her persistent efforts.

runners_data.name: Midnight Lir
runners_data.note: Stable companion to Keep The Gold under Michael Dods; though shown in midfield on the map, this horse is a genuine hold-up type nudged forward due to the crowded rear-of-field — consistent 5f good-ground form with 0W2P from 10 similar runs, tongue-tie and breast girth fitted, and the 15-day turnaround with a strong T14 rate of 3/27 is a positive angle.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Midnight Lir does at least bring experience of today's trip and going, and three consecutive fourths suggest consistency without conviction; 134 lb from stall 10 won't make life easier for a gelding yet to find the winner's enclosure.

runners_data.name: South Parade
runners_data.note: Fahey-trained 5yo whose natural style is rear-of-field but is shown in midfield due to the volume of hold-up types in this race; placed at 5f on good ground earlier this season, though a 3/5f good record showing 1W3P comes with the caveat that a style mismatch may prevent him getting his preferred ground-up run.
runners_data.comment: Returned to form with a third last time out after a sequence of disappointments, and South Parade has run over today's trip and going before — but she remains winless in recent starts and connections saddle her from a stable that has been firing blanks of late.

runners_data.name: Harry Mole
runners_data.note: The field's clearest prominent second-string after King Of The Jungle; Hollinshead's 4yo has been placed in three of his last five over this exact 5f good-ground profile and Dougie Costello is an excellent booking for a horse who needs to press forward quickly from the gate — no style-fit concerns apply here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Harry Mole does bring consistent placing form — third last time out, and seconds two and three starts back — but that habit of finishing close without getting the job done is the concern; has run over today's trip and going, at least, and returns on a fresh 14-day break.

runners_data.name: Keep The Gold
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse wearing a hood (hg:p) who is placed in midfield on the map due to the glut of closers in this race; two recent second-place finishes over 5f on good ground give some encouragement, but the 33-day gap since last run and a sliding OR suggest he may need this run to sharpen.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Keep The Gold does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and 33 days between runs suggests he returns fresh; however, a ninth last time out makes him hard to fancy from stall nine off 130 lb.

runners_data.name: Falcon Queen
runners_data.note: 3yo hold-up type for R Mike Smith fitted with a hood (hg:h); poor recent form string (8-6-9-8-4 over 6f mostly) and only 3 similar-going runs in sample with 0W0P — genuinely needs a step up in form to get involved and the style redistribution further limits her prospects of finding a clear passage.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with finishes no better than fourth in recent outings, Falcon Queen faces a stiff task from stall 12 carrying 129 lb — experience over today's trip is the one minor consolation for a filly who looks hard to fancy at these weights.

runners_data.name: Supremissy
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's lightly-raced 3yo who won over this 5f good-ground combination earlier in her career; a 47-day break is notable, but a T14 rate of 5/27 is one of the stronger trainer angles in the race — nonetheless, her natural rear-of-field style in a crowded field of closers makes getting a clean run a real challenge.
runners_data.comment: Supremissy has been inconsistent in recent starts — ninth and an unseated rider feature in her last five — and she ranks 11th of 13 on our figures, making her hard to fancy. She does arrive here a winner last time out and has run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: Royal Duke
runners_data.note: 5yo hold-up horse wearing a hood (hg:p) for R Mike Smith; the best similar-going sample in the field (12/15 runs) with 2W4P is eye-catching but those wins appear to have come at a lower OR than the current mark of 46 suggests — the style crowding at the rear makes a clean late run difficult to guarantee.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with a run of fifths and sixths dominating his recent figures, Royal Duke offers little encouragement — though a third six starts back shows he can at least threaten the frame, and experience over today's trip and going is genuinely in his favour.

runners_data.name: Summerstorms Dream
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's 4yo hold-up type back 12 days after her last run; form string (3-5-7-7-2) over predominantly 6f trips raises a mild distance concern on 5f, and 0W2P from 8 similar-going runs means she is yet to prove herself convincingly at this trip — squeezed into midfield on the map, she is unlikely to secure an ideal position.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with a sixth last time out bookending a patchy recent record, Summerstorms Dream faces a stiff ask ranked last on our figures; the experience over today's trip and going, plus a return after just 12 days, offer slim encouragement, but a trainer firing at 5% compounds the concern.

races.paceDynamic: King Of The Jungle is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in a 13-runner 5f handicap on good ground at Ayr, he is set to bowl along in front at a controlled, sustainable gallop that rarely invites early pressure. This creates a single-file, processional pace shape where the tempo is dictated rather than fought over, and the rail-to-finish straight at Ayr rewards those who can track the pace and pick it up sharply inside the final furlong. Harry Mole is the only other prominent-type likely to sit close enough to the early fractions to exert any counter-pressure, meaning the first two furlongs should be relatively unhurried. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Midnight Lir, South Parade, Falcon Queen, Keep The Gold, Supremissy, Royal Duke and Summerstorms Dream are all genuine hold-up horses crammed into a field without the pace to stretch them out; many will end up closer than their true style dictates, muddying the closing stages rather than producing a clean late sweep. This race shape most favours prominent-tracking horses who can sit just behind King Of The Jungle, travel into the race naturally, and produce a decisive move two furlongs out — Hi Lord and Startling, both effective hold-up types capable of travelling prominently off a steady pace, fit that bill best.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If King Of The Jungle sets a steady, uncontested pace and prominent-tracking types move smoothly into contention from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: King Of The Jungle dictates from the front at a comfortable tempo, preserving energy, while Harry Mole and any horse who secures a clean position just off the pace arrive with a meaningful advantage at the furlong marker; the steady fractions mean no late burn-out at the front and a decisive kick from close-up wins it.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Hold-Ups Swamp
scenarios.trigger: If King Of The Jungle goes too slow and the field concertinas, allowing the genuine hold-up horses to get competitive positions and launch a mass finish.
scenarios.body: The overly steady tempo brings the entire field within striking range entering the final furlong, turning the race into a blanket sprint finish where the in-form hold-up horses find daylight; Startling, with three placed efforts on good Ayr-type ground, and Midnight Lir's consistent 5f form make them each capable of threading through.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If King Of The Jungle is allowed such a soft lead that the pace is genuinely false and he simply never gets headed.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing or able to apply pressure at any stage, King Of The Jungle controls every fraction and his rivals find themselves shuffled back or unable to close the gap manufactured in the first two furlongs; his recent winning form at 5f on good ground and his T14 trainer strike rate supports this as a live chance that cannot be completely dismissed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wide Draw, Drifters Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If a high-drawn horse avoids the early scrimmage, finds a clear passage on the outside and picks up the tired early pace in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: With 13 runners on 5f at Ayr, low draws can find themselves boxed in behind a moderate gallop and struggle for a clean run, while a well-drawn horse on the outer secures unimpeded racing room and arrives late with momentum; Water Of Leith and Harb, both experienced 5f hold-up types, are most capable of exploiting this if the rail side becomes congested.

watchPoints.text: King Of The Jungle (front-runner) — watch whether Billy Garritty elects to bowl along at a genuinely fast pace or dawdles; if the tempo is deceptively slow, every hold-up horse in the field gets back into the race and his winning chance is undermined.

Harry Mole — Dougie Costello must secure a prominent position quickly from the gate; if a 13-runner field crowds him back past the first furlong, his entire tactical advantage as the race's clearest tracking horse is lost.

Startling (hg:b) — the hood has coincided with a sequence of placed efforts but no win; watch for any signs of interference or traffic issues in the closing stages given the high volume of hold-up types likely to converge on the same ground inside the final furlong.

Midnight Lir and South Parade — both are true closers who will be ridden from further back than the map shows; if they are forced to race in midfield against their instincts due to the crowded pace shape, monitor whether they find clear daylight or get shuffled wide in the straight.

Supremissy — the 47-day break and Iain Jardine's T14 rate of 5/27 make her one of the more interesting in-form trainer angles; watch whether she is ridden with early urgency or allowed to drift into her natural hold-up role, which would likely leave her with too much to do over 5f.

races.name: Book Ladbrokes Ayr Gold Cup Ladies Day Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Tiger
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a win over 10f on good ground and placed effort at 12f on soft; Ryan Kavanagh's 3lb claim is useful but the horse's habit of finishing from off the pace requires a stronger gallop than Faeberon is likely to set.|
runners_data.comment: Tiger arrives on the back of a win last time out and a second two starts back, boasting distance and going experience and an 85 rating that marks him out as the class act in this field; the concern is a swift six-day turnaround carrying 147 lb from stall 8.

runners_data.name: Mr Lincoln
runners_data.note: Stays well with two placings at 17f and 16f on good ground, but OR=75 is his highest weight in a while and Andrew Mullen faces the challenge of getting him competitive from a deep hold-up berth if the tempo does not truly test the leaders.|
runners_data.comment:
Placed third last time out and second two starts back, Mr Lincoln brings solid recent form into this, and has run over today's trip and going before. Yet to win in his last five starts, but drawn in stall 13 carrying 142 lb, he looks the one to follow on profile.
