runners_data.name: Draupnir
runners_data.note: The only genuine prominent runner aside from the leader; Billy Garritty should find a natural position just off Faeberon's shoulder, and a horse with three recent placings on good ground over 7-9f may be underestimated at this longer 1m2f trip.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last five starts, Draupnir does bring distance and going experience to the table, and his speed rating of 81 offers mild encouragement, but an unplaced latest effort and a seventh before that give him plenty to prove from stall six.

runners_data.name: Geo
runners_data.note: A consistent placer with 14 runs on good ground and five places from them, so conditions suit well; however this genuine hold-up horse has been mapped to midfield due to the volume of closers in the field, meaning it is unlikely to race in its most effective position.|
runners_data.comment: Geo has placed in four of her last six starts, including third last time out and a second two starts back, and she has run over today's trip and going before; yet to win in recent starts and with her trainer in a lean spell at 5%, the 137 lb burden makes this tough.

runners_data.name: Pol Roger
runners_data.note: Placed three times at 10f on good and soft, and the trip is squarely in his wheelhouse; despite those credentials, his natural sit-and-kick style means Sean Kirrane will be battling for a position further back than ideal given the congestion of closers.|
runners_data.comment: Placed third two starts back and runner-up three starts back, Pol Roger has been knocking on the door in recent starts but remains yet to win, and while he has experience over today's trip and going, 136 lb is a stern burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Dryburgh
runners_data.note: A 3yo with three places at 10f on good ground, which fits well; the 64-day absence is a notable flag, and while his form profile suggests he handles this track type, Sam James will need a stronger gallop than expected to launch a winning challenge from off the pace.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts but has placed three times in that spell, including a second last time out; he has run over today's trip and going before, though 64 days off and 134 lb from stall 10 are factors to weigh against him.

runners_data.name: Unchartedterritory
runners_data.note: Most recent win came over 9f on soft ground, but three previous runs at 10f on good suggest this trip and surface are fine; Lewis Edmunds will look to slot in just behind midfield and the 60-day break is worth monitoring.|
runners_data.comment: Unchartedterritory arrives on the back of a win last time out, bringing both distance and going experience to the table, and his rating of 76 gives him a solid claim; the main risk is that 60 days off the track leaves his fitness slightly open to question.

runners_data.name: Faeberon
runners_data.note: The race-shaper — his recent win and a string of placed efforts suggest Dougie Costello has a horse in form; the Simon & Ed Crisford-trained 3yo has the role of controlling front runner and the flat 1m2f at Ayr is an uncomplicated canvas for him, though his overall good-ground form is thin (2 runs).|
runners_data.comment: Faeberon arrives as a live contender, a winner last time out and with experience of today's trip and conditions — the main question is whether 41 days off the track has left him short of peak sharpness.

runners_data.name: Mayor Of Maghera
runners_data.note: Won over 9f on good ground last time out and is proven at that trip; a genuine hold-up horse whose best form comes when finishing through beaten rivals, but the crowded closer's berth means James Sullivan may not get the clear run that style depends upon.|
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back sixth and seventh suggest Mayor Of Maghera is in poor form right now, and ranked 11 of 13 on our figures he's hard to fancy; a winner three starts back offers slim hope, and he has experience of today's going.

runners_data.name: Natzor
runners_data.note: Tagged as a horse that fades in finishes, which is an obvious concern for a hold-up type in a race where a modest gallop gives the leaders an even greater edge; Barry McHugh faces an uphill task getting this OR=60 horse competitive in a bunched rear group.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with an eighth and a ninth among recent efforts, Natzor is hard to fancy down in tenth of thirteen on our rankings despite having run over today's trip and going; he is fit enough on a 10-day turnaround and carries 127 lb from stall four.

runners_data.name: Phantom Shadow
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 10f on good ground and has placed at the same trip, so conditions and distance align neatly; Jason Hart rides a horse with genuine recent form, and if the gallop does quicken, Phantom Shadow's finishing speed makes it the most dangerous of the redistributed closers.|
runners_data.comment: Phantom Shadow is hard to fancy ranked 12 of 13 on our figures, and a fifth and eighth in recent starts undermine his claims despite a win last time out; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 19 days is a fair freshness angle.

runners_data.name: Path To Peace
runners_data.note: Very limited form — just three career runs, all resulting in mid-to-back finishes — and tagged as a horse that fades in the finish; the hold-up style combined with a lack of racecourse experience is a significant disadvantage against more battle-hardened rivals.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, with a sixth the best of a modest recent sequence, Path To Peace faces a stiff task from stall 12 carrying 126 lb — and a rating of 46 leaves her well held on our figures in a field of 13.

runners_data.name: Annandale
runners_data.note: An 8yo with excellent consistency at 11-13f on good ground — four places from five at those trips — but is running here from a midfield slot rather than its natural rearmost position; Lauren Young's 5lb claim is an offset, and the longer straight at Ayr does at least give late runners more time to find their stride.|

runners_data.name: Ibn Altheeb
runners_data.note: Headgear-fitted 3yo (hood/blinkers) with a recent fourth at 11f on good ground; Jack Nicholls' 3lb claim is a positive but the horse's form line shows him as a middle-distance hold-up type who will need to overcome the positional squeeze that affects all closers in this field.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Ibn Altheeb does at least bring distance and going experience to this, and a fourth-placed effort last time out offers modest encouragement — though our rating of 73 suggests he faces a stiff task from stall 11 off 125 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Faeberon is the lone confirmed front runner and, with no meaningful pace rival to press him, Dougie Costello can dictate a controlled, honest gallop over this 1m2f trip on good ground — a tempo that is sustainable rather than searching. Draupnir is the only other runner with a prominent tag and will likely track Faeberon into second position, giving the leader a degree of cover without genuine harassment. Behind them, the field is dominated by hold-up horses, but the data confirms more genuine sit-and-wait types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear: Geo, Pol Roger, Phantom Shadow, Mayor Of Maghera, Annandale and Ibn Altheeb are all true closers redistibuted into midfield slots, meaning several will be racing out of their natural role. A steady, front-runner-controlled pace on a flat, galloping track like Ayr overwhelmingly favours the horse who secures an early position and travels into the race — the tactical verdict is clear: prominent racers who can dictate or sit just off the pace are best served here, while closers forced to detach from their usual rear berth face an uphill task if the gallop is not strong enough to string out the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Faeberon Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Faeberon leads at his own tempo and no rival has the pace or inclination to seriously pressurise him through the early stages.
scenarios.body: Dougie Costello sets a measured pace, allowing Faeberon to conserve energy and build on his recent return to form; at 1m2f on a flat galloping track with a field of hold-up horses, an uncontested lead is a significant tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Mow Down Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Faeberon sets a stronger gallop than expected, burning energy early and leaving himself vulnerable to a sustained late challenge from behind.
scenarios.body: The pace unravels in the final two furlongs and the handful of genuine closers who managed to find a realistic midfield position power through; horses with strong finishing form on good ground become the primary threats.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent or midfield tracker travels powerfully throughout and has just enough left to collar Faeberon inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Draupnir or an off-the-pace tracker who gets a perfect economical trip launches from second or third and catches the leader who has been committed for some time; the good ground suits a horse with a clean, economical action.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Sweeps Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely stronger than expected and the entire field strings out, creating racing room for deep closers to finish through beaten horses.
scenarios.body: A true hold-up runner who successfully found a legitimate rear position produces a sweeping run in the straight; this is the least likely shape given that most hold-up types are forced out of their natural role.

watchPoints.text: Faeberon's early position is critical — if Dougie Costello is allowed to stride clear without a challenge in the first two furlongs, the controlled pace he sets may prove impossible to reel in over the final three.|

Phantom Shadow is the most dangerous hold-up horse in the race given a win last time out at the right trip and going; Jason Hart should be monitored for whether he can find a genuine midfield slot rather than being squeezed to the very rear.|

The cluster of redistributed closers — Geo, Pol Roger, Mayor Of Maghera, Annandale and Ibn Altheeb — all competing for real estate at the back of the field creates a risk of interference and traffic trouble in the straight; watch for horses blocked or forced wide on the home turn.|
Dryburgh's 64-day absence and Unchartedterritory's 60-day layoff both warrant market watching at the off — if either drifts meaningfully, fitness concerns are likely being priced in by connections.|

races.name: Unite Ewing Hope's Happy Retirement Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Hale End
runners_data.note: Won over this C&D trip on Good last time out and clearly goes well fresh at 19 days; wears headgear and prominent style suits the early scrimmage but the competitive prominent picture means he may get squeezed for position.
runners_data.comment: Hale End won last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, but that seventh the start before is a concern, and carrying 130 lb from stall five leaves him needing to find improvement to trouble the principals.

runners_data.name: Count Palatine
runners_data.note: 57-day break is notable and his recent form shows struggles at 7f on Good; steps back to 8f which suits, but his last five races include several disappointing efforts and he has done nothing on this going profile in recent outings.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with only a third two runs back and a second five runs back to show for it, Count Palatine returns after 57 days and faces a stiff task ranked eighth of ten — though he has run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: Jannas Journey
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator ridden by 5lb claimer Lauren Young; won over this exact C&D trip 23 days ago and that course-and-distance form combined with a true wait-and-pounce style means the contested pace scenario suits her profile directly.
runners_data.comment: Jannas Journey has been inconsistent in her last six starts, winning one start back but finishing fourth last time out, and her record either side of that success does little to inspire — she's ranked ninth of ten on our figures. The trainer's current 5% strike rate is a further dampener, though she has run over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Military Leader
runners_data.note: In excellent form with two consecutive wins on Good, but this is a horse who naturally wants to race prominently — in a field this stacked with pace-hungry types he is unlikely to secure that berth and will be racing outside his comfort zone wherever he slots in.
runners_data.comment: Military Leader arrives with experience over today's trip and going, and two wins in his last five starts give him some profile — but ranked last of ten on our figures, he faces a stiff ask, with a third three starts back his deepest recent placing.

runners_data.name: Milteye
runners_data.note: One of the two confirmed front-runners and the most likely pace-setter; 50-day absence and recent soft-ground form may mean peak fitness is a question, but he has the profile to dictate and his Ethan Tindall booking at 5lb is worth noting for the trainer's low-volume yard.
runners_data.comment: Milteye has won twice in his last five starts, including a victory one start back, and he brings both distance and going experience to the table; the main concern is a 50-day absence that leaves his fitness an open question.

runners_data.name: Breakdancer
runners_data.note: Has run well in place without winning from prominent positions; recent form on Tapeta and all-weather surfaces makes his turf Good-ground effectiveness slightly opaque, though he did finish second and third over 8f on Good in his last two turf runs.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Breakdancer nevertheless shows consistency with a second and third in that sequence, and has experience of today's trip and going; carrying 132 lb from stall one, his rating of 86 suggests he holds claims, though his recent fourth is a modest launching pad.

runners_data.name: High Point
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner but his recent form comes entirely over 12-16f on softish ground — this 8f trip on Good is a dramatic change in conditions and trip, and he may not have the speed to sustain a pace-setting role at this distance, making his front-running credentials suspect.
runners_data.comment: High Point won one start back but has been unplaced either side of that success, leaving him a frustrating each-way proposition; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 130 lb from stall two, and his rating of 84 suggests modest improvement is possible.

runners_data.name: Theoryofeverything
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner at OR 87 and a consistent hold-up performer; five recent runs all over 8f on Good showing solid placed efforts, though no win in those outings — this genuine closer fits the race shape if the pace holds up, and Jason Hart is a strong booking.
runners_data.comment: Theoryofeverything has run over today's trip and going, and our rating puts him narrowly top of these on raw ability — yet he remains winless in his last five starts, so the market will want signs that a fifth, fourth and fifth represent a genuine upward trend before fully trusting him at 137 lb from stall 10.

runners_data.name: Walsingham
runners_data.note: Three wins from eight runs on Good and ran over this C&D trip in his last two starts; his prominent style could see him caught in the traffic war but his course form is the best in the field and Billy Garritty rides with good local knowledge.

runners_data.name: Bravais
runners_data.note: 92-day absence is significant and his last five runs show only one placed effort on soft-ish surfaces; a genuine hold-up type whose form has tailed off, and the lengthy break plus soft-form profile makes his ability to benefit from the expected race shape uncertain.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Bravais nonetheless carries an eye-catching rating of 96 — well clear of his official mark of 85 — and has experience over today's trip and conditions; the risk is that three consecutive unplaced efforts and a 92-day absence must be overcome.

races.paceDynamic: Milteye and High Point are both confirmed front-runners and will clash for the lead from the off, creating a genuinely contested pace over Ayr's flat mile on Good ground. With four runners — Hale End, Count Palatine, Breakdancer, and Walsingham — all seeking prominent positions behind them, the early stages will be busy and crowded, compressing the front of the field and making clean passage difficult between the 2f and 3f pole. The field contains more pace-seeking types than the map can accommodate naturally: Military Leader is a genuine prominent racer who is unlikely to secure that berth and has been redistributed to midfield on the map, meaning the prominent positions will be fiercely contested and some will be shuffled back involuntarily. This contested, honest gallop on a flat track strongly favours horses who can travel mid-to-rear without losing ground, then pick off tiring rivals in the straight — the hold-up profile, or horses versatile enough to track at the back of the prominent group in a race that truly sets up for late finishers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Blows Up, Closers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Milteye and High Point burn each other off early and the prominent group is stretched, setting a strong enough gallop to compromise all pace-presser stamina reserves.
scenarios.body: The two leaders trade blows through the first half-mile and the prominent quartet run themselves into trouble, leaving the closing stretch open for those who saved ground; on Good going over a fair Ayr mile the gallop does not need to be extreme for the lead pair to tie each other up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Steadies, Front Stays
scenarios.trigger: If one of Milteye or High Point capitulates quickly, leaving the other to control a calmer, steadier tempo that suits prominent runners into the straight.
scenarios.body: A single front-runner finding their own rhythm and controlling the fractions would mean the pace fails to punish those on or near the speed, and a prominent racer travelling comfortably can sustain their effort to the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Group Splits Honours
scenarios.trigger: If the early contest between the leaders is fierce but brief, with Milteye or High Point dropping away sharply and a prominent tracker like Walsingham or Breakdancer inheriting a perfect stalking position.
scenarios.body: The best-placed prominent survivor avoids the worst of the early traffic and arrives on the heels of a fading leader in the final furlong with clear daylight; Walsingham's strong Good-ground form and three wins at the distance support this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Disaster, Lucky Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion causes sustained interference 2-3 furlongs out, bunching and checking multiple runners and gifting a clear-running horse an uncontested run through.
scenarios.body: With four runners hunting three or four prominent slots, a pileup of checking and switching is a genuine risk, and whoever escapes cleanest — possibly a midfield type finding a gap — benefits from rivals losing momentum at the crucial point.

watchPoints.text: Milteye and High Point are on a direct collision course for the lead — watch the first two furlongs to see which gives way, because if neither does the pace will be genuinely strong and compress stamina reserves throughout the prominent group.

The prominent corridor is dangerously congested with Hale End, Count Palatine, Breakdancer, and Walsingham all chasing the same two or three berths — significant traffic risk at the 2-3f mark as they bunch and check behind the leaders.

Military Leader has the form to be competitive but will almost certainly be forced to race outside his natural prominent role — watch how Sam James places him in the first half-mile, as being too far back removes his key tactical weapon.

High Point's suitability for this trip and going is a genuine question mark — if he fades sharply after setting or contesting the early pace, he could cause interference to the pack just as the straight begins.

Jannas Journey's 5lb claim with Lauren Young is relevant in a tight handicap — if she travels smoothly in rear and times her run correctly the combination of the allowance and the contested pace shape could make her look well treated at her current OR.

races.name: Christmas Parties At Western House Hotel Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Mr Cool
runners_data.note: Won most recently over this exact course and distance on Good ground and brings strong sim-going form (8/15, 1W4P); Charlie Johnston in decent 14-day form (5/44) and Oliver Stammers takes over, but as a natural prominent racer operating in lead role here, its chance is shaped entirely by how long the controlled tempo holds up.
runners_data.comment: Mr Cool shaped well when winning last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions; drawn in stall eight carrying 143 lb, he arrives fresh on a 12-day turnaround and his profile makes him our pick, despite sitting below the top-rated on official figures.

runners_data.name: Annie Edson Taylor
runners_data.note: Phillip Makin's runner returns after 52 days off (tongue-tie worn) and her sole win in recent history came over this trip on Good ground; a genuine hold-up operator whose last good run (1st, 6f, Good) shows she can deliver fresh, and Sam James adds class in the saddle.
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back but has been below-par either side of that success, and 52 days off the track adds a fitness query; she has run over today's trip and going, and carries 139 lb from stall three.

runners_data.name: Impressor
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran fitted with a hood and returns after 59 days; hold-up style is authentic and sim-going form on Good is modest (5/15, 0W2P), while the lack of a win on the surface in recent outings tempers expectations despite his place consistency at 6f.
runners_data.comment: Impressor showed up well with a third two starts back and our rating of 78 — highest among the 13 runners — marks him as a genuine threat; yet to win in recent starts, and the 59-day absence is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Kelpie Grey
runners_data.note: Paul Mulrennan rides this prominent-style runner for Jim Goldie, whose yard is 2/40 in the last 14 days; six recent runs on Good ground (8/15, 0W3P) show consistent placing without a win, and he is likely to sit second behind Mr Cool and hope for a tactical benefit if the pace is truly modest.
runners_data.comment: Kelpie Grey has run over today's trip and going before, and his rating of 73 — eleven pounds clear of his official mark — suggests he's well treated on his best form; fresh off a 12-day break and drawn in stall six, the main concern is a trainer firing at just 5% in the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Thunderstorm Katie
runners_data.note: Lauren Young (5lb claim) partners this genuine closer for Goldie, fresh from just seven days ago; her real habit is to race at the rear and finish with a sustained run, but the crowded hold-up group means she is likely to race closer to midfield than she would choose — temper expectations accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked tenth of thirteen on our figures, Thunderstorm Katie faces a stiff task, her trainer striking at just 5% over the past fortnight; she has run over today's distance and going before, and that recent second two starts back offers a crumb of comfort.

runners_data.name: Taaklam
runners_data.note: Harriet Bethell's three-year-old is lightly exposed at 6f on Good (2/8 sim-going) and showed consecutive places on Tapeta, suggesting the yard is building him towards this surface; Aiden Brookes takes the ride and he is one of the hold-up types who could genuinely find clear air from a midfield position.
runners_data.comment: Taaklam caught the eye with a second three starts back and shaped with promise when fifth two starts back, and he has experience over today's trip and going; the concern is that he has been winless in his last five starts and must bounce back from a seventh last time out.

runners_data.name: Masai Angel
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey send this three-year-old, who has placed once on Good going (2/4 sim-going) and showed a 3rd over 6f on Good recently; a natural finisher, the busy hold-up group means she will likely find herself racing closer than ideal — Jack Garritty must work hard for daylight.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and with a trainer in dire form at 1/42 over the past fortnight, Masai Angel faces a stiff ask here; third two starts back offers some encouragement, and he has run over today's trip and going, drawing from stall two on a rating of 62.

runners_data.name: Whiskey Kisses
runners_data.note: R Mike Smith's three-year-old showed back-to-back 3rds on Good at 6f in recent form and holds sim-going placed form (5/10, 0W3P); Greg Fairley rides and, as a true hold-up horse, she sits in a natural hold-up berth and her consistency at this trip on this surface makes her credible.
runners_data.comment: Whiskey Kisses has been placed third in each of her last two starts, showing consistent mid-division form, though she remains winless in recent starts; she has run over today's trip and going before, and her rating of 68 offers a touch of encouragement from stall 11 carrying 133 lb.

runners_data.name: Elemma
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey's filly has limited form (4 runs, 0W) but her most recent start was a 4th over 6f on Good, and Billy Garritty partners; a hold-up horse by nature pushed into midfield territory by the crowded rear, her lack of a win and short form profile make her the more speculative of the Fahey pair here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, with a string of unplaced efforts and a trainer firing at just 2% over the past fortnight, Elemma is hard to fancy; she has run over today's trip and going before, but that's about the extent of the encouragement here.

runners_data.name: Highfield Sunshine
runners_data.note: John & Sean Quinn's four-year-old has strong sim-going form for a hold-up type (8/15, 0W4P) and Jason Hart takes the ride; the horse's best runs have come over 6f on Good, though recent efforts have been modest, and being a genuine closer forced to race in midfield by the sheer volume of hold-up horses is a tactical inconvenience.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Highfield Sunshine at least has experience over today's trip and going, and a 17-day turnaround leaves her fresh enough — though a fifth and two unplaced efforts in recent starts suggest she'll need to find improvement from stall one off 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Ukiyo
runners_data.note: Andrew Kinirons sends this five-year-old after 50 days off (T14: 0/5 — no wins for the trainer in the last fortnight); M.P. Sheehy rides and, while his 2nd over 7f on Good and a win on Good ground stand out, his most recent runs have been disappointing — the hold-up style is genuine and he gets a real rear berth here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Ukiyo does show some encouragement — a third two starts back and a second four starts back — though the eighth last time out after 50 days off is a concern; she has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 66 suggests she retains ability.

runners_data.name: Doon The Glen
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's six-year-old wears a visor and comes back on just 12 days' rest with a recent win over 6f on Good (1st, 6f, Good in hist); Barry McHugh rides and the horse's sim-going record (11/15, 1W3P) is arguably the best in the field for this surface and trip, making him one to respect despite a low OR.
runners_data.comment: Beaten well last time out after winning two starts back, Doon The Glen faces a stiff ask ranked 12 of 13 on our figures, and a trainer firing at just 5% in the past fortnight does little to inspire confidence — experience over today's trip and going is the main positive.

runners_data.name: Lanarra
runners_data.note: R Mike Smith's three-year-old has shown consistent placed form including a 2nd and 3rd on Good ground (6/9 sim-going) and carries the lightest weight (120lbs); Andrew Mullen rides and, as the lowest-rated runner in the field, the hold-up style is genuine and the weight advantage in a handicap makes her an unexposed type worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 11 of 13 on our figures, Lanarra faces a stiff ask at a rating of 54, and her recent record of just one win in her last five starts offers limited encouragement — though she has run over today's trip and going, and returns fit on a 12-day turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: Mr Cool is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rivals to pressure him, he is expected to bowl along at a sustainable clip on Good ground over six furlongs at Ayr. Kelpie Grey is the only other runner mapped prominently and will likely track Mr Cool, but with no horse willing to push the tempo hard, the pace is set to be honest rather than searching. This controlled, single-pace scenario plays directly into the hands of hold-up horses who can conserve energy and pick up in the final two furlongs — provided they can navigate from their forced midfield positions. The field contains significantly more true hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear; Annie Edson Taylor, Taaklam and Whiskey Kisses are the runners most likely to secure genuine hold-up berths, while Thunderstorm Katie, Masai Angel, Elemma, Highfield Sunshine, Ukiyo, Doon The Glen and Lanarra are all natural hold-up horses redistributed to midfield because the rear of the field is overcrowded. The dominant tactical verdict is that closers and hold-up types with proven ability to deliver a late run on Good ground will be favoured by this relatively uncontested, controlled pace shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Cool sets a fair but uncontested tempo and the genuine hold-up runners find clear runs in the straight.
scenarios.body: Mr Cool rolls along without being threatened, the pace stays honest enough that hold-up horses with a clear run can reel in the leaders in the final furlong; the Good ground rewards those with a sustained finish rather than a sprint burst.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Two Dictate, Hold On
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Cool and Kelpie Grey dominate the race and the pace is so moderate that they steal an unassailable advantage before the field can close.
scenarios.body: With no pressure from behind, the leading pair coast around the bend and into the straight with a significant cushion; the hold-up types, many forced into midfield rather than their natural rear positions, cannot generate enough momentum to reel them in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Suits Improvers
scenarios.trigger: If the overcrowded midfield creates interference in the straight and only horses with the clearest runs deliver their challenge.
scenarios.body: The unusually large cluster of hold-up types redistributed to midfield creates a congested pack, and only those with the sharpest jockeys finding gaps emerge; runners drawn wide or with enterprising riders are best placed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Cool's uncontested lead is faster than it appears and the field, strung out chasing, leaves the door open for a fresh-legged outsider to finish best of all.
scenarios.body: A scenario driven by tactical misreading sees the majority of the field misjudge their challenge, allowing a horse with fresh legs, a competitive OR and proven Good-ground form to emerge late from an unlikely position.

watchPoints.text: Doon The Glen wears a visor and carries the best sim-going record in the field (11/15, 1W3P on Good/6f); Barry McHugh must find a clear run from hold-up territory but if he does, this horse is arriving in the best form of his recent career.

The overcrowded hold-up group — at least seven genuine closers compressed into midfield — creates a significant risk of interference and traffic in the straight; watch for horses drawn wide (Lanarra, Whiskey Kisses) who may find space others cannot.

Mr Cool's uncontested lead could be deceptive — if Kelpie Grey sits too close and a slow tempo develops, the hold-up runners in a bunched midfield may find the deficit too large to bridge in just six furlongs on flat Ayr ground.

Annie Edson Taylor returns after 52 days off for Phillip Makin — the trainer's 14-day strike rate of 1/6 is modest, but the tongue-tie and the fact her last win came fresh over this exact trip on Good ground suggests the yard has targeted this spot.

Lanarra carries 120lbs — the lightest burden in the race — and has placed in six of her last nine runs on Good-equivalent going; Andrew Mullen's positioning in the early stages could be decisive if she gets the clearest run of the hold-up group.

races.name: Book The Ladbrokes Ayr Gold Cup Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Stoic Poet
runners_data.note: A hold-up type for Iain Jardine and M. P. Sheehy, returning after 64 days off; similar-going form reads poorly (0 wins, 0 places from 8 runs on Good) and a 3yo taking on older horses with no recent Good-ground confidence makes this a tough ask.
runners_data.comment: Stoic Poet caught the eye with a second two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, so conditions shouldn't be against him; yet to win in his last five starts, though 64 days off the track is the main query heading into this.

runners_data.name: Milford Grange
runners_data.note: Consistent placer with three placed efforts from seven runs on similar going, but a genuine hold-up horse pushed into a midfield slot here due to traffic — Billy Garritty will need the race to fall perfectly and the field to thin out to produce anything like a natural finish.
runners_data.comment: Milford Grange has run over today's trip and going, and placed second on three occasions in recent starts, yet he's winless in his last six and back-to-back disappointing efforts — eighth and sixth — make him hard to fancy without improvement returning.

runners_data.name: Supreme Clarets
runners_data.note: Consistent 3yo with five placed efforts from twelve runs on comparable ground, including three times at 7f on Good; Warren Fentiman (3lb claim) helps at the weights, though being a natural closer forced to race further forward than ideal in this shape blunts the finishing effort.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last six starts, Supreme Clarets does bring distance and going experience to the table, and second finishes two and three starts back show he's competitive; however, a trainer strike-rate of just 2% over the past fortnight is a concern at 131 lb from stall 3.

runners_data.name: Yaaser
runners_data.note: An 8yo for Jim Goldie with two places from fifteen similar-going runs, last out just 7 days ago which is a slight freshness concern; his deeper hold-up style is his natural mode but in a field this cluttered he will struggle to find the daylight he needs at 7f.
runners_data.comment: Yaaser has been winless in his last six starts, though back-to-back thirds show he isn't disgraced; the trainer's current 5% strike rate from 40 runners is a real concern, and ranked tenth of thirteen on our figures, he faces a stiff ask from stall 12 carrying 130 lb.

runners_data.name: Tap Dancer
runners_data.note: Another Goldie hold-up specialist, this one stepping back to 7f from 10f attempts that have not worked (7th and 6th at longer trips); his Good-ground placings have come at 7-8f but the crowded midfield position means his late run may arrive too late.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts with three sevenths in recent form, Tap Dancer faces an uphill task, and a trainer running at just 5% over the past fortnight offers little encouragement; she has run over today's trip and going before, at least.

runners_data.name: Yy Spirit
runners_data.note: A 3yo lightly raced hold-up type for Susan Corbett, returning after 99 days off with a win on Standard ground over 6f and no turf Good-ground form at all (0W0P from 1 similar-going start); the absence and uncertain going profile are both concerns.
runners_data.comment: A winner three starts back offers the sole encouragement here, but she has been unplaced either side of it and returns after 99 days off. Has run over today's trip, though her figures rank her among the outsiders in this field.

runners_data.name: Sanafi Zabeel
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Jim Goldie who will press hard for the lead; boasts the field's best similar-going record (1 win, 4 places from 7 runs on Good) and was out just 7 days ago, suggesting the stable is targeting this race — if he gets a solo lead he is dangerous.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 12 of 13 on our figures, Sanafi Zabeel is hard to fancy off a tough 136 lb burden from stall 13, and his trainer's woeful 5% strike rate in recent weeks adds little confidence — though he does return quickly on familiar going.

runners_data.name: Circle Of Trust
runners_data.note: Returned to form impressively last time (won at 7f on Soft), wearing a hood; Kevin Ryan runner with Good-ground placed form at this trip — a genuine hold-up type whose recent win suggests confidence, though form at 7f on proper Good is limited (0W0P from 4 attempts).
runners_data.comment: Placed second two starts back and a winner last time out, Circle of Trust arrives on a 49-day break carrying 135 lb from stall 8; he has run over today's trip and going before, though that ninth three starts back tempers expectations slightly.

runners_data.name: Ubetterseethis
runners_data.note: A 3yo hold-up type for Craig Lidster, last seen finishing 4th after a 57-day break; has a win and six places on similar going but those came predominantly at 8f and Soft — the step down to 7f on Good is a slight query.

runners_data.name: Highfield Viking
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for John & Sean Quinn, wearing blinkers; 11 runs on similar going with 2 wins and 5 places from 15, giving him the best raw prominent-style record in the field — Jason Hart knows him well and the 55-day freshen-up could be ideal for a horse that runs best fresh.
runners_data.comment: Highfield Viking shaped with promise when third five starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going keeps him firmly in the mix from stall one carrying 140 lb — though winless in his last five starts, that recent dip in form is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Runninsonofagun
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner in excellent form (2nd, 3rd, 1st in last three) for Tristan Davidson, with Jack Garritty booked; Good-ground record is solid (1W5P from 15 runs) and he is 12 days since last run, which is a comfortable turnaround — the key pace-setter in this race.
runners_data.comment: Placed in four of his last six starts — second last time out and a winner three starts back — Runninsonofagun arrives fresh on 12 days' rest with distance and going experience to call on, though his ranking of ninth in the field and 139 lb burden suggest he faces a stiff ask here.

runners_data.name: Black Storm
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse wearing blinkers for Katie Scott, placed four times from seven Good-ground runs at 7f; 30 days since last run is fine, but like several others, being pushed into midfield rather than a true rear position compromises the finishing burst he needs.
runners_data.comment: Black Storm has been knocking at the door in recent starts — third last time out and a second three starts back show he's consistently hitting the frame, and he has experience over today's trip and conditions. The main risk is that he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Phoenix Of Dreams
runners_data.note: A genuine closer for John & Sean Quinn, also wearing a hood, returning after 102 days off; his entire recent form base is on Standard turf at 7f and his similar-going record on Turf Good is sparse (0W0P from just 1 run) — the layoff combined with the going uncertainty makes him a risky proposition despite the talent.
runners_data.comment: Phoenix Of Dreams landed a win four starts back and was third last time out, but his absence of 102 days and a middling speed rating of 68 temper expectations; he has run over today's trip and going, though stall 11 is where he breaks from under 138 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Runninsonofagun and Sanafi Zabeel are the two confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over this 7f on Good ground at Ayr, creating a genuine, honest gallop rather than a falsely run race. Runninsonofagun has been in fine form (132 in last run) and will be keen to get across early; Sanafi Zabeel, trained by Jim Goldie who runs three in this race, will press him and ensure the pace does not relent. Highfield Viking is the one prominent-style horse capable of tracking the leaders in a natural position, giving him a tactical edge over the large cluster of hold-up types behind. This field holds significantly more hold-up types than can all get their natural position — Milford Grange, Black Storm, Phoenix Of Dreams, Supreme Clarets, Yaaser, Tap Dancer and others are all genuine closers but will find themselves bunched in midfield or worse, unable to produce their characteristic late runs cleanly. The contested pace and honest gallop on Good ground at Ayr over 7f strongly favours a horse that can track the pace in a prominent position or pounce from just off the leaders — pure hold-up horses face a maximum-traffic scenario and a race shape that may not set up ideally for them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Two Fight, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Runninsonofagun and Sanafi Zabeel burn each other up contesting the lead, a horse positioned just off the pace in third or fourth inherits maximum momentum.
scenarios.body: The contested early gallop will see the front two tire inside the final furlong, handing a decisive advantage to any horse that has travelled smoothly in their slipstream; Highfield Viking, with his prominent style and course-form at 7f on Good, is ideally positioned to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Pace-Setter Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Runninsonofagun asserts early and Sanafi Zabeel cannot sustain the challenge, allowing a single horse to dictate a controlled, honest gallop.
scenarios.body: A solo front-runner setting his own rhythm over 7f on Good ground at Ayr can conserve enough energy to hold on, particularly from a low draw in a big field; Runninsonofagun's recent winning form and good-ground record make him the chief beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong throughout and creates enough of a gap that a well-positioned midfield horse finds a seam in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Supreme Clarets and Milford Grange both have placed form on similar Good ground at 7f and could benefit if traffic parts in the final two furlongs; however, both are true hold-up types redistributed to midfield due to the crowded rear, so their natural finishing kick may be partially compromised by a less-than-ideal position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp Tired Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If the front two implode spectacularly and a wall of hold-up horses descends en masse in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: This scenario is the least likely given that so many genuine closers are forced into midfield, unable to produce a true hold-up finish; Phoenix Of Dreams and Black Storm, if they can find clear daylight late, are the best of the deep closers on form at this trip.

watchPoints.text: Runninsonofagun and Sanafi Zabeel will duel for the lead from the break — watch the first furlong closely, as whichever horse asserts first and forces the other to concede will significantly alter the complexion of the race and the energy expenditure of both.

Highfield Viking is the only natural prominent-style horse outside the two front-runners; Jason Hart will need to position him immediately behind the pace in the first two furlongs — if he gets shuffled back into the pack he loses his primary tactical advantage.

The large cluster of hold-up types (Milford Grange, Black Storm, Phoenix Of Dreams, Supreme Clarets, Yaaser, Tap Dancer) will be jostling for the same midfield positions at the break; watch for crowding on the rail and any horses that get hampered or checked in the early stages, as it could compromise their entire race.
Sanafi Zabeel ran just 7 days ago — watch how freely he travels in the early stages, as a horse returning quickly that over-exerts in a pace duel is vulnerable to tying up before the line.

Phoenix Of Dreams is 102 days off the track and has no meaningful Good-ground turf form — watch the market move in the hour before the race as an indicator of whether the Quinn yard consider him ready to perform on unfamiliar ground conditions.

races.name: Festive Day Dancing At Ayr Racecourse Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Wicklow Way
runners_data.note: Won most recently over 10f on Standard, handles Good well (sim-going 9/14) and is held up by Jack Garritty — needs a strong pace collapse to get into it and the race shape makes that unlikely at Ayr over 1m2f.

runners_data.name: Charencey
runners_data.note: Ryan Kavanagh (3lb claim) rides a horse with two recent second-place finishes at 10-12f on Good, making him arguably the most in-form runner — though he sits in the hold-up pack and will need a clear run in the straight to deploy his finishing kick.
runners_data.comment: Charencey has been a model of consistency in recent starts, finishing second in each of his last two outings, and with experience over today's distance and going, he looks the one to beat here from stall 3 — albeit still seeking that elusive first win.

runners_data.name: Falaise Blanc
runners_data.note: Ideally suited by this trip and distance profile with four places from five recent starts over 12-13f on Good — Jake Dickson's 5lb claim gives a weight edge and a forward racing style means he should slot into second or third early, putting him in the ideal position to challenge Sassy Glory late.
runners_data.comment: Falaise Blanc showed consistency with seconds two and three starts back, but a seventh last time out tempers expectations; yet to win in recent starts, he has distance and going experience and is fit enough on an eight-day turnaround, though his official mark of 46 suggests he faces a stiff task from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Golden Valour
runners_data.note: A ten-year-old with a win and two places in similar going conditions (10/15 sim-going), but his natural hold-up style means he ends up mapped further forward than he would like; the STYLE_FIT score of 0.92 reflects the mismatch and his chance should be tempered accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Golden Valour does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and a third three starts back shows he can hit the frame; carrying 135 lb from stall one, he looks a tough ask at a rating of 48.

runners_data.name: One More Bottle
runners_data.note: Barry McHugh rides a horse whose recent runs on Good (just 4/15 sim-going) are noticeably fewer and less positive than the rest of the field — a genuine hold-up type bumped into a midfield slot by the crowded profile, visor headgear noted, modest recent form limits expectations.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, One More Bottle nonetheless rates higher than his official mark of 49 suggests and arrives here on a sharp 12-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and going; the risk is that his recent form simply offers no encouragement.

runners_data.name: Patrick Street
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on Good and has placed three times from five recent runs — a confirmed stayer who travels prominently and should push forward into third or fourth early; M.P. Sheehy rides and this horse has the distance credentials to be dangerous if Sassy Glory ties up.
runners_data.comment: Patrick Street won two starts back but has been in and out of form, finishing fifth last time out; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 135 lb from stall 13, and his rating places him mid-division in a competitive field.

runners_data.name: Sassy Glory
runners_data.note: The race-shaper: the only confirmed front-runner in the field, wearing a visor, and with four place finishes from six recent runs including a win on Standard — Jason Hart will take this horse straight to the lead and the uncontested pace makes her the pivotal horse in every scenario.
runners_data.comment: Sassy Glory won two starts back and was second three starts back, showing a clear vein of form at this level, and she returns fit on 14 days' rest with distance and going experience to call on; the risk is that unplaced effort last time must be forgiven.

runners_data.name: Storm On Jura
runners_data.note: Lauren Young (5lb) rides a horse flagged as fading in the finish, with no wins or places in recent outings (0W0P) — a true hold-up horse shifted into the midfield map position by the crowded rearward contingent, and the finish-fade flag makes this a hard horse to support here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with finishes no better than fourth in recent outings, Storm On Jura heads here ranked near the foot of our figures and with a trainer in poor form; she has run over today's trip and going, but it's hard to make a strong case from stall ten off 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Zebra Star
runners_data.note: Shay Farmer (5lb) takes the ride on a six-year-old with three placing runs but limited Good-ground experience (10/15 sim-going skewed) — his natural inclination to hold up means he shares the crowded rearward cluster and needs things to go very right to get involved.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked ninth of 13 on our ratings, Zebra Star faces a stiff ask, though a fourth two starts back hints at some ability; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 34 days off should leave her fresh.

runners_data.name: Flying Moonlight
runners_data.note: A lightly-raced three-year-old trained by Mrs A M Thomson (no runners in the last 14 days) with back-to-back third-place finishes on Good — Sean Kirrane partners a horse stepping into a competitive handicap field, and while the form is honest the redistribution to midfield means he is racing away from his ideal tactical spot.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a pair of thirds his only encouragement, Flying Moonlight has struggled badly in between and our figures rank him near the foot of the field; the going experience and 33-day break offer slim positives, but he's hard to fancy at these weights.

runners_data.name: Raise The Stakes
runners_data.note: Two solid Good-ground placings at 10f and a visor suggests headgear is working, but a 43-day layoff is notable and the finish-fade flag is a concern; Greg Fairley rides a horse who needs to come from well off the pace yet has only limited recent Good-ground evidence (2/7 sim-going) to suggest he can deliver late.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Raise The Stakes has shown some encouragement with a third last time out and a second two starts back, but the 43-day absence, a lowly official rating of 49, and our figures ranking him tenth of thirteen make him hard to fancy here.

runners_data.name: Resdev Time
runners_data.note: Billy Garritty rides a three-year-old with consistent Good-ground form (9/12 sim-going) and two recent places over 10-12f — the true racing style is hold-up but the numbers suggest a horse who keeps grinding without quite winning; the midfield slot is slightly away from his preferred rear position.
runners_data.comment: Resdev Time's third three starts back is her chief credential here, and experience over today's trip and going lends quiet confidence; winless in her last six, however, she'll need to rediscover that form to threaten at the finish.

runners_data.name: Sanny Doo
runners_data.note: Paul Mulrennan takes the ride on Jim Goldie's three-year-old who has shown no wins or places in recent starts (0W0P across five runs) and recorded only a 5/8 sim-going score — the least credentialled runner in the field and the redistribution to midfield compounds an already difficult task.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with finishes no better than fourth in recent outings, Sanny Doo faces a stiff ask here — ranked last on our figures and carrying 127 lb from stall 8 for a trainer striking at just 5% lately; experience over today's trip and going is the sole consolation.

races.paceDynamic: Sassy Glory is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of 13 and will stride to the lead unchallenged from the off, setting a genuine but controllable pace over 1m2f on Good ground at Ayr — a track where front-runners with a clear rail hold can be very hard to catch. The rest of the field is overwhelmingly made up of hold-up types, meaning the pack behind will be chasing one lead horse rather than fighting for the front, leaving the pace scenario unusually clean and predictable. Horses like One More Bottle, Storm On Jura, Resdev Time, Charencey, and Raise The Stakes are genuine hold-up or prominent types who cannot all get their natural position in this shape — Falaise Blanc and Patrick Street are the most likely to press forward into the slipstream and secure the second and third positions on the track. The race shape strongly favours Sassy Glory's hold on the front end and any horse with the ability to travel prominently in second or third, as late closers face a long, honest gallop with little compression or bunching to give them momentum.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sassy Glory Front-Runs Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Sassy Glory dictates fully unchallenged and the Good ground holds a sound but not brutal pace, leaving closers with too much to find.
scenarios.body: Sassy Glory controls every fraction from the front and, with no rivals pressuring, builds a lead that is extremely difficult to close down over 1m2f; the hold-up-heavy field chases on a flat course with no sharp bend to help late closers get into the race quickly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest and one of the closer-travelling prominent types collars Sassy Glory inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Falaise Blanc or Patrick Street, sitting just behind Sassy Glory throughout, benefit from a true pace and arrive with a strong cruising speed to head the leader close home; both have strong records of placing from a forward position and suit this shape perfectly on Good turf.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than anticipated and the field is strung out with a gap opening up the wide outside for a finishing run.
scenarios.body: A well-positioned hold-up horse — most likely Charencey or Raise The Stakes, who have the best recent form credentials from behind — finds clear running in the straight and runs on strongly past tired rivals; note both carry the STYLE_FIT caveat meaning they are racing out of their easiest position and this scenario is inherently less likely to materialise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — No Clean Winner
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types press forward early disrupting the anticipated clean solo lead, creating a frantic pace that collapses the field into a bunch finish.
scenarios.body: Sassy Glory's advantage is compromised by unexpected pressure from one or more redistributed horses forcing their natural position, causing the field to race in a compressed group and opening the door for the lowest-weighted runners to benefit from the chaos; Wicklow Way and Flying Moonlight, both unexposed at this trip, represent the upside in this unlikely shape.

watchPoints.text: Sassy Glory holds a monopoly on the front-running role — watch whether Jason Hart goes hard immediately to build a buffer or attempts to control the pace conservatively, as that decision will dictate whether the closers ever get into the race.

Falaise Blanc is the biggest danger to Sassy Glory if Jake Dickson angles him forward early — watch whether the 5lb claimer can secure the pocket in second or third, because from there Falaise Blanc's strong placing record over this trip becomes very dangerous.

Patrick Street showed stamina when winning over 12f on Good and M.P. Sheehy may ride prominently — monitor the opening quarter-mile to see if this horse travels up behind the leader, which would set up a genuine late challenge from a well-credentialled stayer.

Storm On Jura carries a fades-in-finish flag and has a 33-day break — if Lauren Young attempts to push forward out of character to avoid the congested rearward group, it could unexpectedly pressurize Sassy Glory's lead and alter the entire pace shape.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up types (One More Bottle, Resdev Time, Zebra Star, Sanny Doo, Flying Moonlight) all competing for midfield real estate could cause significant traffic and interference in the straight — horses with cleaner outside routes like Charencey and Raise The Stakes may benefit if the rail becomes congested.
